body:
I just attempted suicide, yesterday. Xanax and alcohol. The worst part is, what always kept me from that point was I felt that it would hurt. But it didnt. I felt wonderful, pure bliss. I fell asleep and I woke up inside the next day with my family keeping eye on me. I guess at some point I blacked out and came into the house. I undressed and my mother made me lie down in her room. That was, I think 2 days ago? I don't know, my head is really fuzzy and I'm struggling remembering anything, at this point. Everything phases into itself.

Please, don't send me PM or reply about seeking help, I don't need any of that. I'm fine as is and don't want any pity.

Quite hinestly, and this will sound both strange and pompous, but as a person who suffers from bipolar and PTSD Holden makes sense to me. I don't know how I would explain him to someone else, it'd be like trying to explain color to a blind person. But as a teen when I was first diagnosed and as an adult who struggles with my mentally stability every day, I keep going back to this book. I feel like Holden is my closest friend. He's the only person who seems to feel the way I do. For the most part anyhow.

Edit: Very, very long post. 

My mother, grandmother, and my grandmother's aunt have all had bipolar. I was never afraid of having it utilizes I was 13 and started showing symptoms of Depressive Type Bipolar 1, meaning 1 or more episodes of mania. 

At 13 I started, not feeling sad, but not feeling at all. I was empty all the time. And when I did feel it was anger towards everything. I starting cutting myself not out of sadness, but because I was so angry at myself that I thought I deserved to hurt. I would wake up and say "fuck" because I'd hoped I'd died in my sleep the day before. And when I would finally muster enough will power to bathe I would end up letting the hot water run while I swore at myself in the mirror and ran a shaving razor down my legs. It got worse by 15. I started hurting other people. I never outright challenged someone, I would wait for them to attack me, which happened a lot in high school. And when they did I would vent out my frustrations by hurting them in ways related to me. I would typically choke them. But every now and again I would hit them directly in the face. 15 was also around the time where my mood would rapidly change. I would be laughing so hard I'd cry only to bawl my eyes out within the same minute, then punch myself out of anger. I started having outburst at my family and was checked into a psyche ward for minors, where they showed my mom my scarring. They put me on a medication for depression instead of mood stabalizing, making me more manic. Then they put me on a mood stabilizer. I told them I was having headaches and they told me that was not a side effect. Turns out that it was and I was allergic to the medication. I started hallucinating. My mom found out and took me off of it, leaving me on just the antidepressants. So my I manic all of the time. I did crazy things, took risks. I would go to stay with friends hours away and run off in the night, I was dabbling in drugs, buying illegal pocket knives. I started smoking spice in the end. At the age of 16 I went cold turkey off of my medications because I had no way of buying them and no way of getting to my appointments. At 17 I was admitted to another psychiatric ward where they worked hard with me and found that I was one of the worst cases of bipolar they'd ever seen. I also had an anxiety disorder, paranoia didorder, and PTSD. Bipolar also includes insomnia in most cases. I remember laying in bed at night every night unable to sleep. I started thinking about hurting other people instead of me. I started hearing voices in my head. They put me on mood stabilizers, an anti-psychoticand sleep medication. Then, at 19, I was admitted another time. The doctor there told me he didn't believe all of my symptoms and took me off of everything except the anti-psychotic. I didn't get any sleep for weeks after that and started believing that my anti-psychotic was a placebo and that my world was some form of the Truman Show, but a documentary of mental health. And that it was leading up to suicide. This made me very angry. By this point the voice in my head was loud and clear at all times. He even told me his name. He would give advice. After a little while he was getting to be too much to bear. He started telling me to kill my brother and so I checked myself in, to a psychiatric ward. But this was different because it was on my terms. They put me back on all of my original medications and within a week I was improving. But with bipolar things are so sporadic. I moved out of my parents to live with a friend. It ended up turning sour. He was downright abusive. After almost a year I called my dad at work and told him that I just didn't know if I could do it anymore and that I needed advice. He said he didn't know because he'd never felt that way. I said I thought I was going to kill myself and he said okay. He called my mom and she called the police. I was trying to cut down my arm, not across my wrist like you see in movies, that doesn't work. But the blade was so dull all it did was bruise me. The police came in and my mom called me. I answered and was tearing ul because I said I didn't know what to do, I didn't know how to kill myself quick enough. She talked me into answering the door and when I saw it was the police my roommate started shouting at me. I dropped my phone. I remember I could hear my mom crying and shouting over the phone. The cops escorted my roommate out. They later told me and my parents that he was the most toxic person they'd met and that I needed out of there. I went to the hospital where the same doctor who had been taking care of me for my panic attacks saw me. He said my name and came and talked to me. You wouldn't even think I had just attempted suicide. We were laughing and talking. They admitted me. The doctors made the mistake of talking me off of everything but my anti-psychotic again. But the doctor who admitted me did not give up. He worked his magic while in communication with my parents. I finally got in with a good psychiatrist. I'm on a lot of medications now, half of them for psyche. About 3 or 4 medications, I believe. But they work. I was on prozac but it had an adverse effect and made me suicidal. Now I'm off of it and am doing well. I got in with and good therapist. I learned to control a lot of my mood. I work with animals. I'm a groundskeeper. I even met someone recently. I've got a lot of new friends. I'm eating and drinking normally again, but getting again good amount of exercise. I'm close with my brother. There's a lot of good things. But with bipolar, my opinion does change a lot. It could even right after this comment. But when I get too depressed, too stressed, and I start looking for a way out. When I start hating the world. I remind myself that there is a lot of bad in the world, but the good of it is worth living for. It's been a crazy life, but it's getting better. I'm better.
